items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: Then I could play the blues anyway, because I knew Jesse Crump's things

ctx.x: That was his...(Laughter). After I played his big number I went into my "Dallas Stomp"...you know what I mean...the blues, you know, this here, you know what I mean. I could really stomp because this girl had really...a week with her and I realized that that's what rhythm was, you know, that the rhythm was part of it...you didn't have girls, so it was the stomping... you know what I mean...it was the stomping in here and the combination of the piano and humming and all, then you were...then when I got through…

you know, you see these guitar parts and banjo parts where they have the names of the chords, you know? All right, I devised a way that I could take a piece of newspaper and write the chords on a piece of newspaper. And then I learned the structure of the... what the tonic note was, and the seventh...well, I'd learned all that from Miss Pitman, you know. And I learned how to...passing tones, and playing blues and Boogie-Woogie movement, but we didn't call it that, you see. Walking bass...
